activity.nil: an activity of service "{service}" has a nil function
allow.empty: {node}: a permission names an action and a resource
allow.nil-policy: {node} is allowed by a nil policy: give Allow the policy that grants the permission
app.nil-service: the app mounts a nil service
auth.credentials.none: the credentials type {type} has no field tagged cookie:"…" or header:"…"
auth.credentials.not-struct: the credentials type {type} must be a struct whose fields are tagged cookie:"…" or header:"…"
auth.credentials.source: field {field} of the credentials is read from the {in}: credentials come from a cookie or a header
auth.credentials.untagged: field {field} of the credentials is not tagged: credentials come from a cookie:"…" or a header:"…"
auth.missing: endpoint {endpoint} asks for authentication, but the app mounts no auth handler: declare one with Service.AuthHandler
auth.missing-for: {node} asks for a user, but the app mounts no auth handler: declare one with Service.AuthHandler
auth.nil: auth handler "{name}" has a nil handler
auth.two: the app has two auth handlers, {first} and {second}: an app authenticates its callers one way
auth.two-at: the app has two auth handlers, {first} (declared at {file}:{line}) and {second}: an app authenticates its callers one way
authorize.nil: {node} is authorized by a nil function
authorize.twice: {node} is given two Authorize: give it one function, which may call others
binary.contract: binary {binary}: {from} talks to {to} through "{contract}", which needs two declared roles and a versioned contract, render/v1
binary.name: binary "{name}" is not a name: lower-case letters, digits and dashes
binary.role-name: binary {binary}: role "{name}" is not a name: lower-case letters, digits and dashes
binary.role-nil: binary {binary}: role {role} is run by a nil app
binary.role-twice: binary {binary}: role {role} is declared twice, or selected by the same arguments as another
bind.nil: app.Bind binds port {port} to nil: give it an operation of the port's types
bind.nil-port: app.Bind is given a nil port
bind.port: app.Bind binds port {port} to port {op}: a port calls an operation, never another port
bind.port-unmounted: app.Bind binds port {port}, of service "{service}", which the app does not mount
bind.scope: app.Mount of module {module} binds port {port}, which is not the module's: bind it among the app's own options
bind.unmounted: app.Bind binds port {port} to {op}, of service "{service}", which the app does not mount: mount it, or bind the port to another operation
classify.erased-type: field {field} is tagged erased but holds a {type}: the framework stamps a time.Time or a *time.Time
classify.history: field {field}: app:"{tag}": history=N keeps from 1 to {max} former values
classify.history-many: field {field} keeps its former values but sits inside a list or a map: an element has no identity from one version to the next, so history=N goes on a field of the record itself
classify.looks-personal: field {field} reads like personal data but has no class: tag it app:"personal", or app:"public" if it holds nothing personal
classify.secret-moderated: field {field}: app:"{tag}": nobody sees a secret, so nobody moderates it
classify.secret-personal: field {field} is tagged secret but its name reads like personal data: secret means a credential, which the framework never exports and the register lists as one — tag personal data app:"personal": still sealed at rest and never shown, and exported and erased with its person
classify.special-plain: field {field}: app:"{tag}": special data is always sealed at rest, never plain
classify.subject-class: field {field}: app:"{tag}": a subject identifies a person, so it cannot be {class}
classify.subject-many: field {field} is a subject inside a list or a map: a record is about one person
classify.subject-twice: {type} has two subject fields, {first} and {second}: a record is about one person
classify.tag-renamed: {field} is tagged kit:"{value}", which the framework no longer reads: tag it app:"{value}"
classify.subject-type: field {field} is a subject but holds a {type}: a subject is a string or an integer
classify.two-classes: field {field}: app:"{tag}" gives two classes, {first} and {second}: a field holds one kind of data
classify.unknown: field {field}: app:"{tag}" has the unknown word "{word}": a field takes one class — public, personal, special or secret — and the options subject, moderated, plain, erased and history=N
cli.default-twice: CLI commands {node} and {other} are both the default command: Main can run only one
cli.nil: CLI command "{name}" has a nil function
cli.reserved: CLI command {node} takes the name "{name}", which Main keeps for itself: name it otherwise
command.limits: command {command}: MaxDeliveries and Parallelism must be at least 1
command.not-queued: command {command} is not queued: MaxDeliveries, Parallelism, Drain, Settle, Lease and AutoExtend apply to a command declared with app.Queued()
command.queued-result: command {command} is queued: it answers nothing, so its result must be app.Empty, not {type}
config.memory: no data directory: stores and queues live in memory and are lost on restart; set {prefix}_DATA_DIR
secret.reserved: secret or database URL "{name}" would be read from {variable}, a variable of the framework's own: name it otherwise
config.renamed: {old} is set, but the framework no longer reads it: it reads {new} — rename it where the product is deployed
config.studio-missing: dev asks for the Studio, which the framework serves only when the program imports {package}: add import _ "{package}"
config.studio-production: the Studio is never served in production: it exposes the source and live traffic
consumer.failed: the consumer of {node} failed, and the framework restarts it after a backoff: {detail}
consumer.file-queue-left: the queue of {node} now lives on database "{database}": the messages its file queue under the data directory still holds are not delivered — drain them with the release before, or copy them to the database: data copy --to {database}
database.kept-twice: {what} is kept by two databases, "{first}" and "{second}": a thing lives in one database
database.own-prefix: database "{name}": a database's name cannot start with "{prefix}", which the framework keeps for its own
database.max-open: the pool needs a ceiling above 0
database.memory-store: database "{database}" keeps store {store} by name, but the store is kept in memory (app.InMemory)
database.name: database "{name}": a database's name is 1 to {max} lower-case letters, digits and dashes, starting and ending with a letter or a digit
database.name-taken: database "{database}" needs the name "{name}" for its URL or its tuning, but {owner} already has it
database.nil-engine: database "{name}" has no engine: give it one from an engine module, postgres.Engine()
database.nil-keep: database "{database}": app.Keeps is given nothing to keep
database.positive: it must be a positive duration
database.sqlite-busy-timeout: the URL of database "{database}" sets a busy timeout of {busy}, which must stay under {setting}, {timeout}: SQLite would give up just as the call ends — lower it, or leave it to the framework
database.sqlite-timeout: {setting} is {timeout}: a SQLite database needs at least {floor}, so that the busy timeout the framework gives it keeps a margin under it
database.table-twice: database "{database}" would keep two of the framework's tables under one name: {tables} — rename one of the nodes
database.tls: the URL of database "{database}" leaves TLS to the driver, which may send in the clear: write its mode in {variable} — sslmode=verify-full for {engine}, or TLS off on a private network
database.two-defaults: databases "{first}" and "{second}" are both declared without app.Keeps: one database keeps every store no other keeps
database.unmounted: database "{database}" keeps {what}, which the app does not mount
database.url-dev: database "{database}" has no URL: its stores stay in the data directory; set {variable} to open it
database.url-invalid: the URL of database "{database}" is not one {engine} reads: check {variable}
database.url-missing: database "{database}" has no URL: set {variable}, or {variable}_FILE naming a file that holds it, or keep it with `{app} secrets set {secret}`
database.url-unreadable: the URL of database "{database}" cannot be read: {detail}
decode.kind: field {field} ({type}) cannot be read from the {in}: use a string, a number, a bool, a time, a duration or a pointer to one
decode.not-struct: the request type {type} is not a struct, so the route wildcards {wildcards} cannot be bound
decode.pointer: field {field} is tagged {in}:"{name}" inside an embedded pointer: embed that struct by value
decode.unbound-wildcard: the route wildcard {{{name}}} is not bound to any field: add a field tagged `path:"{name}"`
decode.unexported: field {field} is tagged {in}:"{name}" but is not exported, so it can never be set
decode.unknown-wildcard: field {field} is bound to the path wildcard {{{name}}}, which the route does not have
endpoint.validate: endpoint "{route}": the validate tags of {type} are not valid: {detail}
expose.any-user: the exposure of {node} is marked app.AnyUser(), but the operation does not require a user: declare app.Auth() on the operation — an exposure authenticates as its operation asks — or mark the exposure app.Anyone()
expose.anyone: the exposure of {node} is marked app.Anyone(), but the operation requires a user: mark it app.AnyUser(), open to any signed-in user
expose.auth: the exposure of {node} asks for authentication itself: declare it on the operation, whose exposures and in-process runs are then checked alike
expose.marked: the exposure of {node} is marked {marker}, but the operation says who may run it (Allow, Authorize): drop the marker, which says an exposure is open on purpose
expose.markers: the exposure of {node} is marked both app.Anyone() and app.AnyUser(): keep the one that says who may run it
expose.open: the exposure of {node} does not say who may run it: give the operation a permission (Allow) or a rule (Authorize), or mark the exposure open on purpose — app.Anyone() for everyone, app.AnyUser() for any signed-in user
index.name: store "{store}": index name "{name}" must start with a letter and use letters, digits, '_', '.' or '-'
index.nil: store "{store}": the index "{name}" has a nil key function
index.type: store "{store}" holds {type}, but the key function of its index "{name}" reads {reads}
job.cron: job "{name}": "{expr}" is not a five-field cron expression
job.period: job "{name}": the period must be positive
key.nil: command {command} is keyed by a nil function
key.twice: command {command} is given two keys: one function names the entity it is about
listener.contract: listener "{name}" speaks "{contract}", which is not a versioned contract: "<name>/v<major>", render/v1
listener.path: listener "{name}" is given a socket path that is not absolute
listener.path-per: listener "{name}" is given both a socket path and SocketPer scopes: the path would ignore them
loop.every: loop "{name}": WakeEvery needs a positive period
loop.topic: loop "{name}": WakeOn has a nil topic
mailer.capture: mailer {mailer} keeps its mail in memory and delivers none: set {prefix}_SMTP_URL (smtp://user:password@host:587?tls=starttls), or {prefix}_SMTP_URL_FILE naming a file that holds it
mailer.max-age-negative: mailer "{name}": its max-age must be a duration of zero or more: 0 sets no age
module.foreign: {node} is declared on {service}, a service of module {module}, from outside its Go module {gomodule}: a product reaches a module through its ports, commands, topics and settings — declare the endpoint on a service of the product
module.foreign-builder: {node}, of module {module}, is given {builder} from outside its Go module {gomodule}: a product gives a module's operation no permission, rule or key of its own — it dispatches the command, or asks the query, from an endpoint of its own, and narrows access there
module.foreign-passwords: {store}, declared at {at}, of module {module}, is given a password policy from outside its Go module {gomodule}: a product puts no policy of its own on a module's store — it sets, changes and verifies the module's passwords through a policy the module declares
module.own-service: module {module} lists {service}, the framework's own service: the framework mounts it itself, in every app that keeps personal data
module.migrations-nowhere: module {module} declares migrations, and no database keeps it: they run on the database that keeps the module — declare one with app.Database
module.migrations-twice: module {module} declares migrations, and two databases keep its stores, "{first}" and "{second}": its set would run on both — keep the module on one of them with app.Keeps
module.name: module name "{name}" must be lower-case letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter
module.name-service: the product's service "{service}" is named like a module the app mounts, declared at {at}: a module's name qualifies its services and its settings — rename the service
module.name-setting: setting "{key}" of {service} is named like a module the app mounts, declared at {at}: "{key}:" in a configuration file is the module's section — rename the setting
module.nil-part: module {module} lists a nil part: a service, or an app.Requires, declared before the module
module.nil-requires: module {module} requires a nil module: app.Requires takes a module declared before it
module.reserved: module name "{name}" is the framework's: "app", "kit", "external" and "schema" — whose version table would be the product's, schema_migrations — are reserved
module.service-own: the app mounts service "{service}" itself, which module {module} lists (declared at {at}): mount the module instead — its services come with it — and take the service out of app.NewApp
module.service-taken: module {module} lists service "{service}", which module {other} lists already: a service is one module's
module.twice: two modules the app mounts are named {module}, declared at {first} and {second}: a module's name qualifies everything it declares, so it is unique in the app
mount.nil: the app mounts a nil module: give App.With or app.Mount a module declared with app.NewModule
mount.only-name: app.Only of module {module} names "{env}", which is not an environment's name: lower-case letters, digits and dashes inside, 63 at most, as {prefix}_ENV names it lower-cased
mount.only-none: module {module} is mounted with app.Only and no environment: it would never be mounted; name the environments, or drop the mount
mount.only-required: module {module} is mounted only in {envs}, but {by}, mounted in {env}, requires it: mount {module} in {env} too, or give {by} the same app.Only
mount.prefix: module {module} is mounted under "{prefix}": a prefix starts and ends with '/', has no space, wildcard, query or fragment, and never lies under /_app/ nor /_kit/
node.name: {kind} name "{name}" must start with a letter and use letters, digits, '_', '.' or '-'
node.setting-name: "{node}": its setting "{setting}" is not a setting's name: 1 to {max} lower-case letters, digits and dashes
operation.validate: {node}: the validate tags of {type} are not valid: {detail}
passwords.history-short: field {field}: app:"history={history}" keeps fewer former values than NotReused({n}) refuses: raise it to {n}, or leave history out — NotReused keeps what it reads
passwords.min-length: a password policy's MinLength({min}) is below {floor}, the fewest characters NIST allows, and only with a second factor
passwords.no-field: store {store}: the password policy's function names no field of the entity: return the address of one of its string fields, reached without a pointer
passwords.no-rate-limit: endpoint {endpoint} sets or changes the passwords of {store} with no rate limit: a change verifies up to NotReused+1 hashes, each slow by design, and tells its caller whether a password was used recently; add app.RateLimitPerClient
passwords.not-reused: a password policy's NotReused({n}) refuses from 1 to {max} former passwords
passwords.not-secret: field {field} of {store} holds a password's hash, but it is not tagged app:"secret": a password policy reads a secret field only
passwords.twice: field {field} of {store} has two password policies: a field has one
policy.breaker-refused: "{port}": its breaker is refused with the values the start resolved — {knob} —: every call would fail; change the setting that gives it
policy.budget-alone: "{port}": it is given a retry budget but neither retries nor hedges: give it app.Retry or app.Hedge, or take the budget off
policy.budget-ratio: it must be a thousandth of a token or more
policy.give-up-within: it must be a duration of zero or more: 0 never gives up
policy.hedge-idempotent: "{port}": a hedge runs its operation more than once for one call: declare app.Idempotent() if it may, or take the hedge off
policy.jitter: it must be full, decorrelated or none
policy.overlap: it must be skip, allow or replace
policy.positive: it must be a positive duration
policy.rate: it must be a number of calls a second above zero
policy.ratio: it must be a share above 0 and at most 1
policy.setting-name: "{node}": its policy's setting "{setting}" is not a setting's name — 1 to {max} lower-case letters, digits and dashes —: the policy runs with the code's values and no configuration reaches it; give the operation a shorter name, with app.Name for an endpoint
policy.setting-twice: "{node}": its policy's setting "{setting}" is declared already: an operation takes one policy of a kind, and two operations of a service whose names spell alike share their settings — rename one, with app.Name for an endpoint
policy.starting-deadline: it must be a duration of zero or more: 0 runs a late fire however late
policy.throttle-k: it must be a number of 1 or more
policy.wait: it must be a duration of zero or more: 0 waits not at all
port.fallback-nil: port {port} has a nil fallback: app.Fallback takes an operation declared before the port
port.fallback-port: port {port} falls back to port {op}: a port calls an operation, never another port
port.fallback-unmounted: port {port} falls back to {op}, of service "{service}", which the app does not mount: mount it, implement the port, or bind it with app.Bind
port.guard-twice: port {port} is guarded twice: give every policy to one Guard
port.implementations: port {port} has several implementations, {implementations}, and no app.Bind: the app chooses one with app.Bind(port, implementation)
port.unbound: port {port} has nothing bound: implement it on a service the app mounts — var _ = Service.Implement(port, handler), the handler a {handler} —, bind it with app.Bind(port, operation), or give it an app.Fallback(operation)
principal.missing: the auth data of {handler} ({type}) does not implement app.Principal: every Allow of {nodes} refuses
privacy.by-product-retention: store "{store}" says the product keeps its retention (app.RetentionByProduct) and gives the framework one (app.EraseAfter, app.EraseAt, app.DeleteAfter or app.DeleteAt): a store's retention is the framework's or the product's — drop one
privacy.delay: store "{store}": the delay of {option} must be positive
privacy.index-key-memory: the framework's index key lives in memory alone and is made again at every start, while what the app keeps persists: after a restart it no longer finds what it referenced before — a hold, a record's own data key, a person's references —, and a database files its index rows again — pin {variable} (openssl rand -base64 32), or keep the secrets on disk ({prefix}_SECRETS=file:<dir> with {prefix}_SECRETS_KEY)
privacy.no-retention: store {store} keeps personal data but says nowhere for how long: declare app.EraseAfter, app.EraseAt, app.DeleteAfter or app.DeleteAt
privacy.no-subject: store {store} keeps personal data, but no field tagged subject says whom a record is about: nobody can have its records exported or erased
privacy.option-type: store "{store}" holds {type}, but the function of its {option} reads {reads}
privacy.rekeyed: store {store}: a record's key is built from personal data, so the framework deleted a record it had to erase: build the key from an identifier
profile.cli-listener: {node} listens, which a CLI command never does: a CLI run ends before any client could connect
profile.http: {node} serves HTTP, which the {profile} profile never does: serve it from a server app, or reach the daemon on a listener
profile.idle: IdleStop is for a daemon, and a positive time: this app's profile is {profile}
profile.server-missing: the app is a server — the default profile — and serves HTTP only when the program imports {package}: add import _ "{package}", or give it the daemon or cli profile
profile.singleton: Singleton scope "{scope}" is not a name: lower-case letters, digits and dashes
profile.unknown: the app declares the profile "{profile}": a profile is server, daemon or cli
replace.nil: app.Replace is given a nil operation
replace.nil-fn: app.Replace replaces {node} with a nil function
replace.not-test: app.Replace replaces {node}, but this program is not a test: a replacement runs only in a binary go test builds
replace.unmounted: app.Replace replaces {node}, of service "{service}", which the app does not mount
retention.invalid: {variable} must be on, dry-run or off
retention.off: {variable}=off: no store erases or deletes its personal data on its own
route.conflict: route "{route}" of {owner} conflicts with another route: {detail}
route.conflict-with: route "{route}" of {owner} conflicts with another route (declared by {other}): {detail}
route.method: route "{route}" must start with an HTTP method in upper case, then one space: "GET /todos"
route.path: route "{route}" must have a path starting with '/', without spaces, query or fragment
route.reserved: route "{route}" is under /_app/ or /_kit/, which the framework reserves for itself
seal.data-key-memory: store {store} keeps sealed data on disk, but the framework's data-key lives in memory and is made again at every start: the next start could not open the data — pin {variable}, or keep the secrets on disk ({prefix}_SECRETS=file:<dir> with {prefix}_SECRETS_KEY)
seal.data-key-size: {variable} must hold exactly {bytes} bytes — a keyring's version is a key —: head -c {bytes} /dev/urandom > file, then {variable}_FILE=file
seal.key-reads: store {store}: its key reads {fields}, which the framework seals: kept in clear at rest, as the key already is in the store's files — build the key from an identifier, or tag the field plain
seal.keys-beside: database {database} keeps the framework's data keys (app.Privacy) beside store {store}, whose data they seal: a dump of it carries both — keep app.Privacy on another database
seal.keys-memory: store {store} keeps sealed data on disk, but the framework's data keys ({keys}) are kept in memory: the next start could not open the data — keep app.Privacy on disk too
seal.rewrap: the framework's data keys could not all be re-wrapped under the newest version of {secret}: {detail}; the older versions are kept meanwhile
secret.bytes: secret "{name}": Generated takes {min} to {max} bytes — 32 for a key — not {bytes}
secret.file-suffix: secret name "{name}" must not end in -file: its variable would end in _FILE, the form that names a file holding a secret
secret.generated-env: secret {secret} is generated, and {prefix}_SECRETS=env keeps nothing the framework can write: set {prefix}_SECRETS=file:<dir> with {prefix}_SECRETS_KEY, or memory to make it again at every start — or pin it with {variable}
secret.keep: secret "{name}": KeepVersions needs at least 2, so that what the version a rotation replaces sealed or signed still opens
secret.own-prefix: secret name "{name}" must not start with "{prefix}": the framework keeps its own secrets under that prefix
secret.name: secret name "{name}" must be 1 to {max} lower-case letters, digits and dashes, starting and ending with a letter or a digit
secret.optional-generated: secret "{name}" is Generated and Optional: the framework makes a generated secret, so it is never absent — drop one of the two
secret.pinned: secret {secret} is pinned by {variable}: the framework uses it as it is and does not rotate it
secret.provided-options: secret "{name}" is provided: RotateEvery and KeepVersions apply to a Generated one
secret.qualified-name: secret "{key}" is kept as "{stored}", longer than {max} characters: shorten the secret's name or the module's
secret.rotate: secret "{name}": RotateEvery needs a positive interval
secret.twice: secret "{name}" is declared by {first} and {second}: a secret's name is its variable, {variable}, so it is unique in the app
secret.unset: secret {secret} is not set: set {variable}, or {variable}_FILE naming a file that holds it
secret.unset-store: secret {secret} is not set: set {variable}, or {variable}_FILE naming a file that holds it, or run the product's secrets set {name}
secrets.key-beside: the secret store's key lies beside it, in the data directory: set {prefix}_SECRETS_KEY to keep it elsewhere
secrets.memory: no data directory: a generated secret lives in memory and is made again at every start; set {prefix}_DATA_DIR or {prefix}_SECRETS
secrets.no-protected-store: this platform has no protected file store: the secrets live in memory, and a generated secret is made again at every start
service.name: service name "{name}" must be lower-case letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter
setting.code-unknown: app.Set names "{key}", which no service declares
setting.env-name: {prefix}_ENV "{env}" cannot name a configuration file: lower-case letters, digits and dashes
setting.file-secret: {file} sets "{key}", a secret: a file is committed and a secret never is — set {variable} where the product runs, or {app} secrets set {key}
setting.file-section: {file}: "{module}:" is module {module}'s section, which maps its settings' names to their values
setting.file-suffix: setting name "{name}" must not end in -file: its variable would end in _FILE, the form that names a file holding a secret
setting.file-format: {file}: the framework reads this format only when the program imports {package}: add import _ "{package}"
setting.files: {files}: one file per environment, in one format
setting.own-prefix: setting name "{name}" must not start with "{prefix}": the framework keeps that prefix
setting.name: setting name "{name}" must be 1 to {max} lower-case letters, digits and dashes, starting and ending with a letter or a digit
setting.positive: setting "{key}" must be a positive duration, for {waiters}
setting.required: setting "{key}" of {service} is required: set {variable}, or "{key}" in {file}
setting.secret-name: setting "{key}" has the name of a secret: the two would share {variable}
setting.reserved: setting "{key}" would be read from {variable}, a variable of the framework's own: name it otherwise
setting.stray: {variable} is set, but no setting or secret of the product reads it
setting.twice: setting "{key}" is declared by {first} and {second}: a name is unique in the app, and its variable is one
setting.variable-twice: setting "{key}" of {second} and "{other}" of {first} share the variable {variable}: rename one of them
smtp.transport: is refused by the SMTP transport: {detail}
static.index: frontend "{name}" has no index.html at its root
static.nil: frontend "{name}" has a nil file system
static.prefix: frontend "{name}": the prefix "{prefix}" must start and end with '/', outside /_app/ and /_kit/
static.root: frontend "{name}": "{root}" is not a directory of its file system
store.nil-key: store "{name}" has a nil key function
store.revisions: store "{store}": app.Revisions({n}) keeps from 1 to {max} former versions of each record
store.trash-name: store "{store}": its trash setting "{setting}" is not a setting's name: 1 to {max} lower-case letters, digits and dashes
store.trash-negative: it must be a duration of zero or more: 0 turns the trash off
store.unconfirmed: a write to {store} stands, but the data directory did not confirm it: it may not survive a power loss
subscription.own-stores: subscription "{name}" is given app.OwnStores, which is a watch's: a topic has no stores to hear
subsystem.missing: {node} needs the framework's {subsystem} subsystem, which this program does not import: add import _ "{package}"
supervision.gave-up: {node} failed more than {restarts} times within {within}: the framework stopped restarting it, and the product is no longer live — its liveness check {check} fails — so that the process is restarted; fix what fails it, or raise its give-up settings
topic.once-nil: topic {topic} is given a nil key by Once: a message published once needs a key
topic.once-twice: topic {topic} is given Once twice: a topic publishes once under one key
transaction.effect: {node}: what a transaction held until its commit could not leave after it — the commit stands: {detail}
transaction.two-databases: {node} writes stores of {databases}: a transaction writes one database, and its write to a second is refused — keep what it writes on one database, or split it
value.bool: is not a boolean: true or false
value.duration: is not a duration with its unit: 90s, 15m, 24h
value.duration-text: is not a duration with its unit, as a text: "90s", "15m", "24h"
value.list: is not a list of texts
value.text: is not a text: quote it
watch.catch-up: the last run of {watch} did not stop cleanly, and its catch-up failed: it is tried again at the next start: {detail}
watch.lost: a write to {store} stands, but the queue of {watch} refused its notice, which is lost: {detail}
watch.mark: watch "{name}" watches "{mark}", which is no mark: app.Personal, app.Special or app.Moderated
watch.replay-partial: {watch}: {notices} notices queued before the replay failed; the watch hears them at the product's next start — run the command again for the rest
watch.replayed: {watch}: {notices} notices queued, one per record of the stores that feed it ({stores}); the watch hears them at the product's next start, at least once
watch.running-mark: the running mark of {watch} cannot be written or removed in the data directory, so a stop that is not clean may go unnoticed: {detail}
workflow.event-name: workflow "{name}": a transition needs a name other than "{event}"
workflow.guard-nil: workflow "{name}": guard transition "{event}" has a nil guard
workflow.hook-failed: an OnTransition hook of {workflow} failed after "{event}" on "{key}": {detail}
workflow.initial: workflow "{name}" has no initial state: call Initial
workflow.instant-nil: workflow "{name}": timer transition "{event}" has a nil instant function
workflow.needs: workflow "{name}" needs a store and a state function
workflow.state-spelled-twice: workflow "{name}": two states are spelled {state}, which the engine would take for one: give each state its own spelling
workflow.timer-nil-setting: workflow "{name}": timer transition "{event}" waits a nil setting
workflow.timer-positive: workflow "{name}": timer transition "{event}" needs a positive duration
